methodology.authors: St Alphonsus's 22 passage-level claims plus Gihr, Le Brun, Guéranger, Dujardin, St Vincent Ferrer and qualified Passion methods are separate voices. No synthetic writing passed as a quotation.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Creation and worship
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The problem is not why man invented sacrifice, but why the creature can owe anything to the Creator. St Alphonsus distinguishes the ends traditionally attributed to sacrifice—adoration, thanksgiving, expiation and petition—and the acts by which an offering is made. Creation makes the first two intelligible; the Fall will make the third urgent. The Eucharist is not simply the most impressive instance of an older ritual category. It is Christ's own offering, which gives the Church's thanksgiving and petition their efficacy.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: At Creation, worship is an obligation and a privilege; after sin, it will also become a plea for reconciliation.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Fall and promised redemption
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The Fall introduces a contradiction into human worship: the creature still owes God honour, yet can no longer approach Him as though nothing had happened. Dujardin reads the opening movement of Mass against Adam's loss of innocence. His interpretation is a spiritual lens, not the original meaning of the Roman opening prayers. The actual Confiteor and Kyrie speak of guilt and mercy, while Genesis establishes why those themes cannot be detached from the history of redemption.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The first sacrifices will expose the question the Fall leaves unresolved: what makes an offering acceptable to God?
limitations: Do not state Introibo or Confiteor were composed to reenact the Fall.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Abel: sacrifice, righteousness and innocent blood
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Abel's offering receives divine favour; the text does not explain its acceptance through a technical ritual formula. Hebrews interprets his offering in terms of faith. Gihr, reading Abel through the Roman Canon, develops a typology of the righteous offerer and the innocent blood that cries out. We must not adopt his additional conjecture that fire descended from heaven: Genesis does not say so. When Supra quae names Abel after the Consecration, it asks us to consider divine acceptance, not equality between an ancient gift and Christ Himself.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The problem of accepted sacrifice persists, but the next figure introduces a stranger element: priesthood without the genealogy of Israel's later priests.

limitations: Genesis 4 does not state that fire consumed Abel's sacrifice: Gihr's fire inference is conjectural.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Melchisedech: bread, wine and priesthood
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: In Genesis, Melchisedech is both king and priest; he brings forth bread and wine and blesses Abraham. The Epistle to the Hebrews returns to the brief episode to explain a priesthood fulfilled in Christ. Gihr interprets the bread and wine sacrificially, following a long Christian tradition, but Genesis 14 does not itself narrate their consecration or explicitly state that they were immolated. This distinction matters because the Mass invokes Melchisedech as a figure of the Eucharistic offering without making his rite identical with the Roman rite.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The mysterious priest meets Abraham before the more painful trial in which Abraham must relinquish the son of promise.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Abraham and Isaac: son of the promise
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The command to offer Isaac challenges the promise made to Abraham: the son through whom the covenant is to continue appears to be demanded back. Abraham is stopped, and Isaac is not killed. Gihr and St Alphonsus read the obedience of Abraham and the beloved son carrying wood as prefiguring Christ, but this becomes intelligible only because the outcomes differ: Isaac is spared while Christ freely undergoes death. Supra quae later names Abraham's sacrifice among the accepted offerings, while the Eucharist presents the one infinitely greater sacrifice.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: What Abraham undergoes privately, Israel will next encounter nationally: deliverance bound to a lamb and its blood.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Passover: blood of deliverance
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: In Exodus 12 the blood of a lamb identifies the households spared in the judgment upon Egypt. The meal is bound to a commanded remembrance and to the departure from bondage. St Alphonsus expressly uses the Paschal lamb among the Old Law's anticipations of Christ's sacrifice. The Christian claim is not that the Roman Agnus Dei simply quotes Exodus, but that Christ is the Paschal Lamb whose death accomplishes a deeper deliverance; the Gospel and St Paul provide the bridge.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The people saved through the sea must still be sustained on their journey; redemption calls for nourishment, not deliverance alone.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Manna: food in the wilderness
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The manna is a gift for a pilgrim people, neither earned nor supplied by their own resources. Yet those who ate it still died. In John 6, Christ sets the true Bread from heaven in deliberate contrast with the manna: His gift is not merely provisional bodily sustenance. The Eucharistic application must be presented through Christ's discourse and Catholic sacramental teaching rather than pretending that Exodus already describes the consecrated Host. This stage prepares Communion, without collapsing the distinction between Israel's history and the sacrament.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: Food for the journey is followed by covenant: a relationship formally sealed with blood.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Sinai: covenant sealed in blood
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: At Sinai, the people assent to the words of the covenant and Moses applies blood in its solemn confirmation. Jeremiah promises a new covenant, not simply a renewal of compliance with the former one. At the Last Supper Christ speaks of His Blood in connection with the new covenant. St Alphonsus reads this in light of the Eucharistic institution and its sacrificial fulfilment. The chalice formula of the 1962 Roman Missal has its own received wording; it is not a quotation copied without change from one biblical account.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The covenant also requires an ordered life of worship: altar, sanctuary, priest and appointed sacrifice.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Sanctuary and ministerial priesthood
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The tabernacle and the later Temple teach that access to God's presence is never treated as a casual activity. Priestly mediation and sacrifice are part of Israel's worship, but the Letter to the Hebrews explains both their dignity and their insufficiency compared with Christ's priesthood. St Alphonsus uses Levitical figures, while later commentators sometimes connect the priest's extended hands at Hanc igitur with the imposition of hands upon a victim. This is symbolic interpretation, not a demonstrable explanation of the gesture's Roman origin. The live scapegoat of Leviticus 16 is sent away rather than slain.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The prophet who sees God's throne hears a hymn that the Roman Mass will actually take into its own words.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Isaiah's heavenly worship
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Isaiah's vision begins not with a description of a temple object but with the holiness of the Lord before whom even the seraphim veil themselves. The Sanctus draws upon this proclamation, joined in Christian worship with the acclamation addressed to Christ on His entry into Jerusalem. The two sources should remain visible. The liturgical text speaks with Scripture's language but is not a continuous quotation from a single episode. The difference between vision and liturgical adaptation is itself a fruitful matter for contemplation.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The same prophet also announces a suffering servant; heavenly holiness will be approached through the sufferings of the innocent.
limitations: Vulgate Isaiah says Dominus Deus exercituum; Roman Sanctus uses Deus Sabaoth, an adapted witness.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Suffering Servant: the innocent victim
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Isaiah's suffering servant bears the iniquities of many without simply being one more animal substitute. St Alphonsus considers such prophecies within the older law's sacrificial figures and turns to Hebrews to explain their fulfilment. The decisive claim of Christian sacrificial theology is that Christ's obedience and self-offering exceed every previous victim. The narrative must let the biblical passage speak in its own context before explaining the Church's interpretation of it as a prophecy of the Passion and its relation to Mass.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: With the need for a definitive sacrifice revealed, prophecy turns outward toward an offering made among the nations.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Prophecy of the pure offering
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Malachi's announcement of a pure offering among the nations belongs first to the prophet's rebuke of corrupt worship. Christian tradition reads its universality and purity in relation to the Eucharistic Sacrifice. Le Brun's preliminary treatise specifically moves from the sacrifices of the old dispensation to Christ, their fulfilment, and then to the Mass. This is a theological reading within tradition, not the claim that the prophet described the Roman Missal's future gestures or textual formulas.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The promise now ceases to be merely a figure or oracle: the divine Son assumes the nature in which He can offer Himself.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Annunciation and Incarnation
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: At the Annunciation, the eternal Son becomes man without ceasing to be God. St Alphonsus treats the Incarnation as the preparation of the victim who will offer Himself freely: a human body is taken for the accomplishment of the Father's will, as Hebrews interprets the mystery. This does not mean the historical sacrifice of Calvary is already finished at Nazareth. The Mass's Credo and the Last Gospel confess the Incarnation in different ritual positions, but the salvation-history journey encounters it at the historical beginning of Christ's earthly life.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The birth of the Word in the flesh is greeted with praise that will become the opening words of a much longer liturgical hymn.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Nativity and angelic Gloria
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The Gloria begins with the proclamation heard by the shepherds at Bethlehem. St Alphonsus notes the scriptural opening, but the hymn that follows is the Church's developed act of praise and petition, not an unaltered transcript of the angels' song. The Nativity therefore contributes actual language to the Mass while the later liturgical text expands its scope to adoration of the Trinity and supplication to the Lamb. This is a stronger connection than treating the priest's posture as an imitation of a shepherd.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The child announced as Saviour will be identified publicly as the Lamb whose sacrifice removes sin.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: John the Baptist calls Christ the Lamb
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: John the Baptist's testimony, 'Lamb of God', is not a general image of innocence. Heard after the Passover narratives and the prophets, it identifies Jesus as the one through whom sin is taken away. The Roman Agnus Dei reuses the Baptist's words but extends them into petitions for mercy and, ordinarily, peace. Their location before Communion belongs to the liturgical arrangement; their theological force comes from the identity of the sacrificed and living Christ.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The Lord whom John identifies will also speak of a bread from heaven radically unlike Israel's temporary nourishment.
limitations: Mass Agnus Dei petitions are liturgical adaptation; distinguish Requiem form.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Christ the living Bread
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: In John 6, Christ links His identity as living Bread with the gift of His flesh for the life of the world; the discourse must be read in full, including the objections and the departure of many listeners. It is not a miniature account of the rite of Communion. The Mass later gives a sacramental form to receiving Christ. The centurion's statement in Matthew 8 supplies a second, different scriptural connection: the Church adapts the language of a servant's healing into the communicant's humble confession of unworthiness.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: Christ's approaching entry into Jerusalem sets the final sequence of His public ministry in motion.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Entry into Jerusalem and Benedictus
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The crowd's cry when Christ enters Jerusalem includes 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.' Within the Sanctus the Church places that acclamation after Isaiah's heavenly hymn. The juxtaposition matters: worshippers bless the coming Messiah while joining the worship of heaven. But the Mass does not present Palm Sunday as though it occurred after Isaiah's vision in one biblical narrative. The two biblical moments are joined liturgically; in this journey, they remain chronologically distinct.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The Lord's arrival leads to the institution of the Eucharist in anticipation of His Passion.
limitations: Do not treat Sanctus and Benedictus as a single biblical quotation.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: The Last Supper and Eucharistic institution
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The evangelists and St Paul witness Christ giving bread and wine as His Body and Blood and commanding the memorial. St Alphonsus treats the Last Supper in explicit relation to sacrifice and the Church's Eucharistic participation; he also distinguishes his own conclusion from an anonymous French writer's account of sacrificial consummation. A serious treatment must preserve this disagreement rather than smoothing it into a single inherited explanation. The sacramental institution anticipates and is inseparable from Calvary, without multiplying historical sacrifices.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The freedom of Christ's offering becomes manifest when He accepts the Father's will in Gethsemane.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Gethsemane and voluntary oblation
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Gethsemane shows that Christ's sacrifice is voluntary obedience, not merely suffering inflicted by others. Hebrews interprets the saving efficacy of His offering through the obedience of His will. St Alphonsus traces the sacrificial purpose of the Incarnation toward this consent and its fulfilment; the Passion-meditation methods of later writers associate particular Mass gestures with this scene. Such associations may aid prayer, but they must remain optional, explicitly attributed, and separate from the historical cause of the gestures.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The obedience accepted in the garden is consummated on Calvary, where all the earlier sacrificial figures are judged by their fulfilment.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Calvary: the unique and perfect sacrifice
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: At Calvary, the true Priest is also the Victim. St Alphonsus sets out the actions traditionally analysed in sacrifice and insists on Christ's once-for-all self-offering, then explains the Eucharist as sacramental participation in that same offering. He argues specifically against locating the fulfilment of every sacrificial act solely in Christ's glorification; the Eucharistic Communion matters to his account. Le Brun likewise makes Christ's unique sacrifice the point toward which prior sacrifices converge. In Mass the one offering is present sacramentally, not repeated as another execution.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The Resurrection does not cancel the Cross; it reveals that the offering of the crucified Lord is victorious and enduring.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Resurrection and Emmaus
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The risen Christ opens the Scriptures to the disciples on the road to Emmaus. Their retrospective understanding parallels the reader's task in the biblical journey: to discern the fulfilment of the earlier figures without rewriting them as if their authors had already seen every later rite. The Canon explicitly remembers the Resurrection in Unde et memores. The connection between Emmaus and Eucharistic Communion is a traditional interpretive reading, but the breaking of bread in Luke 24 cannot by itself be treated as a documentary account of the Roman Mass.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The risen Lord ascends; His priesthood does not cease with His visible departure.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Ascension and permanent priestly mediation
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Christ enters the heavenly sanctuary as the enduring High Priest. St Alphonsus's presentation of priesthood according to Melchisedech links the Psalm and Hebrews, while his reading of Supplices te rogamus records disagreement about the holy Angel: is the figure Christ Himself or angelic ministry carrying the Church's prayers? His own preference should not be attributed to the other interpreter. Nothing in this prayer requires imagining that the consecrated elements are physically transported to heaven.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The exalted Lord sends the Holy Ghost and establishes the Church's continuing sacramental life on earth.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: Pentecost and the Church's Eucharistic life
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: Pentecost forms a worshipping, teaching Church. The primitive community is described as persevering in the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayers. In the Roman Canon, the petitions for the living and the remembrance of saints make sense within this ecclesial unity. Dujardin meditates on Pentecost near the end of Mass, but that spiritual association does not establish an apostolic origin for the priest's final blessing. The Church's Eucharistic life is historical; the private meditation is interpretive.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The Church's sacramental worship anticipates a final communion that the Apocalypse portrays through the Lamb and heavenly worship.

biblicalNarrativeDrafts.title: The Lamb and heavenly Jerusalem
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.narrative: The Apocalypse portrays heavenly worship around the Lamb and a future marriage supper. These images are not a coded description of a terrestrial Roman Mass, yet the Church has long understood her Eucharistic offering and Communion in relation to Christ's heavenly priesthood. St Alphonsus expressly debates where the language of sacrificial completion belongs, warning against treating glorification and Eucharistic participation as interchangeable accounts. The final vision is the goal of the pilgrimage, not a historical episode already completed on a biblical calendar.
biblicalNarrativeDrafts.transitionToNext: The narrative returns to Creation: man's end is communion with God, now understood through the saving priesthood and sacrifice of Christ.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Psalm 42 turns the approach to the altar into a prayer of trust, where its recitation is prescribed. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa042.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: The priest approaches the altar with the words of Psalm 42: “Introibo ad altare Dei.” The psalmist asks God's light and truth to lead him to God's dwelling despite trial and sorrow. The preparation for Mass thus becomes an act of trust: one approaches God to receive his mercy and praise him. Under the 1962 rubrics this psalm is not recited at every Mass, including Masses for the Dead. Le psalmiste demande que la lumière et la vérité de Dieu le conduisent vers sa demeure, malgré l’épreuve et la tristesse. La préparation de la Messe devient ainsi un acte de confiance : on approche de Dieu pour recevoir sa miséricorde et le louer. Ce psaume n’est pas récité à toutes les Messes de 1962, notamment aux Messes des défunts. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa042.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/298.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: The repeated Kyrie is the Church's appeal to the Lord's mercy, not a mere pause before the Gloria. The cries of those who begged Christ for mercy in the Gospel show the faith and need with which we can make this prayer our own. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: La miséricorde au seuil de la Messe [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Le Kyrie répété est la supplication de l'Église à la miséricorde du Seigneur, non une simple attente avant le Gloria. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The Gloria joins the angels' praise at Bethlehem to the Church's adoration of the Trinity. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk002.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: At the Saviour's birth, the angels proclaim God's glory and the peace brought to mankind (Luke 2:14). The Gloria takes up their acclamation and unfolds it into a hymn of praise: the Church blesses the Father, adores the Son, confesses him as the Lamb who takes away the world's sins, and glorifies the Holy Spirit. Its opening adapts Luke's account; the remainder develops that praise in the Church's own hymn. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk002.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/300.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Le Gloria unit la louange des anges à Bethléem à l'adoration de la Sainte Trinité par l'Église. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk002.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: À la naissance du Sauveur, les anges annoncent la gloire de Dieu et la paix apportée aux hommes (Lc 2,14). Le Gloria reprend leur acclamation et la déploie en une grande hymne de louange : l’Église bénit le Père, adore le Fils, le reconnaît comme l’Agneau de Dieu qui enlève les péchés du monde et glorifie le Saint-Esprit. Le début du texte liturgique est adapté du récit de saint Luc ; le reste de l’hymne développe cette louange. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk002.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/300.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: One prayer of the Church [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).

Its words are determined by the Mass being celebrated, sometimes with permitted commemorations. The faithful make this prayer their own through attentive prayer and the response Amen; a general explanation must never substitute a different day's text. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Une seule prière de l'Église [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Dans la Collecte, le prêtre rassemble les demandes de l'Église dans la prière publique propre à la célébration. Ses paroles dépendent de la Messe du jour et, lorsque les rubriques le permettent, des commémoraisons. Les fidèles s'y unissent et la ratifient par l'Amen ; une explication générale ne remplace jamais le texte du jour. [Rite de 1962](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Munda cor meum recalls the purification of Isaiah's lips before the Gospel. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: Before the Gospel, the minister who is to proclaim it prays “Munda cor meum ac labia mea.” He asks God to purify his heart and lips, just as Isaiah's lips were cleansed by the burning coal brought by a seraph (Isaiah 6:5–7). The vision teaches that one who proclaims God's word must first receive purification. At Mass this prayer prepares the priest or deacon to announce the Gospel worthily. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/301.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Le Munda cor meum rappelle la purification des lèvres d'Isaïe avant l'Évangile. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Avant l’Évangile, le ministre qui doit le proclamer prie : « Munda cor meum ac labia mea ». Il demande à Dieu de purifier son cœur et ses lèvres, comme celles du prophète Isaïe furent purifiées par le charbon ardent apporté par un séraphin (Is 6,5–7). La vision biblique manifeste que celui qui annonce la parole de Dieu doit d’abord recevoir sa purification. À la Messe, la prière prépare le prêtre ou le diacre à proclamer dignement l’Évangile. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/301.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The homily explains, it does not replace [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: The sermon may expound the readings, the feast, the doctrine or the Christian life, but it is not a fixed text of the Missal. The Church's worship and the homily therefore require distinct kinds of attention: the prescribed Mass texts retain their own identity even when preaching is brief, absent or extended. Any biblical links from a sermon should belong to that actual sermon, not to an imaginary standard reading. La liturgie et la prédication appellent donc une attention distincte : les textes prescrits de la Messe gardent leur identité, que le sermon soit bref, absent ou développé. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: At the Incarnation in the Creed, we profess that the eternal Word truly became man. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh001.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: At “Et incarnatus est,” the Creed confesses that the eternal Son of God took a true human nature without ceasing to be God. St John expresses this mystery with the words, “The Word was made flesh” (John 1:14). The prescribed genuflection gives visible expression to adoration of the Incarnation. The Creed thus joins the profession of faith to a bodily act of reverence. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh001.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/302.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: À l'Incarnation proclamée dans le Credo, nous confessons que le Verbe éternel s'est vraiment fait homme. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh001.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Lorsque le Credo proclame « Et incarnatus est », l’Église confesse que le Fils éternel de Dieu a pris une véritable nature humaine, sans cesser d’être Dieu. Saint Jean résume ce mystère : « Le Verbe s’est fait chair » (Jn 1,14). La génuflexion prescrite à ces paroles rend visible l’adoration du mystère de l’Incarnation. La Messe demande ainsi que l’intelligence de la foi et l’attitude du corps s’accordent dans la profession du Credo. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh001.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/302.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The Lavabo's Psalm joins the priest's washing to a prayer for purity of heart. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa025.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: As the priest washes his hands at the Offertory, he prays Vulgate Psalm 25: “Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas.” The psalmist loves the Lord's dwelling and longs to remain among those who give him praise. In the Mass, the bodily washing accompanies the desire for purity of soul before the Eucharistic sacrifice. These are actual psalm verses, generally numbered Psalm 26 in modern Bibles. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa025.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/303.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Le psaume du Lavabo unit l'ablution du prêtre à la demande de pureté du cœur. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa025.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: En se lavant les mains à l’Offertoire, le prêtre récite le psaume 25 de la Vulgate : « Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas ». Le psalmiste aime la maison du Seigneur et demande à demeurer parmi ceux qui rendent gloire à Dieu. Dans la Messe, le lavage matériel accompagne le désir d’une âme pure avant de s’approcher du sacrifice eucharistique. Les paroles sont bien celles du psaume, dont la numérotation moderne est généralement 26. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa025.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/303.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: In spiritu humilitatis makes the Offertory an appeal for humble, contrite hearts. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/dan003.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: After offering the chalice, the priest bows and prays “In spiritu humilitatis.” The words come from Azariah's plea in the furnace: deprived of the Temple's place and means of sacrifice, he asks God to receive a humble spirit and contrite heart (Daniel 3:38–40). The Mass takes up this disposition of humility before the Eucharistic sacrifice, whose worth comes from Christ himself. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/dan003.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/303.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: L'In spiritu humilitatis fait de l'Offertoire une supplication de cœurs humbles et contrits. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/dan003.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Après l’offrande du calice, le prêtre s’incline et prie « In spiritu humilitatis ». Ces paroles viennent de la supplication d’Azarias dans la fournaise : le peuple ne possède plus alors le lieu ni les moyens d’offrir les sacrifices du Temple, mais il demande à Dieu d’accueillir un esprit humilié et un cœur contrit (Dn 3,38–40). La Messe reprend cette humble disposition du cœur au seuil du sacrifice eucharistique, qui trouve sa valeur dans le Christ lui-même. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/dan003.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/303.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: At Masses with Offertory incensation, Psalm 140 compares rising incense to prayer. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa140.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: At the Offertory of Masses where incensation is prescribed, the priest prays with Vulgate Psalm 140: “Let my prayer rise before you like incense” (Psalm 140:2). The ascending smoke gives visible expression to the Church's desire that her prayers be received by God. Revelation also depicts incense joined to the prayers of the saints in heavenly worship (Revelation 8:3–4). This incensation depends on the form of Mass and is not part of the ordinary Low Mass. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa140.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/303.png). [Second biblical passage](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/apo008.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Lorsque l'Offertoire comporte l'encensement, le psaume 140 compare l'encens qui monte à la prière. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa140.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: À l’Offertoire des Messes où l’encensement est prescrit, le prêtre prie avec le psaume 140 de la Vulgate : « Que ma prière s’élève devant vous comme l’encens » (Ps 140,2). La fumée qui monte rend visible le désir que les prières de l’Église soient reçues par Dieu. L’Apocalypse décrit également l’encens uni aux prières des saints dans le culte céleste (Ap 8,3–4). Cet encensement dépend du rite célébré et n’appartient pas à la Messe basse ordinaire. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/psa140.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/303.png). [Deuxième passage biblique](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/apo008.htm).

This distinction is important: the baptized unite their prayer, thanksgiving, sufferings and self-offering to the Eucharistic Sacrifice, while the ordained priest performs its sacramental action in the person of Christ. The Secret continues the petition over the prepared offerings and is proper to the celebration. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The Sanctus unites earthly worship with the praise heard by Isaiah and John. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: In a vision, Isaiah hears the seraphim proclaim the Lord's holiness three times (Isaiah 6:3). The Sanctus brings that praise into the Church's worship: heaven and earth are full of God's glory. Revelation describes heavenly beings likewise praising the divine holiness without ceasing (Revelation 4:8). These are distinct visions that illuminate the same adoration. The Mass says “Deus Sabaoth,” where the Clementine Isaiah text has “Deus exercituum.” [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/376.png). studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Le Sanctus unit le culte terrestre à la louange entendue par Isaïe et saint Jean. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Dans une vision, Isaïe entend les séraphins proclamer trois fois la sainteté du Seigneur (Is 6,3). Le Sanctus fait entrer cette louange dans la prière de l’Église : le ciel et la terre sont remplis de la gloire de Dieu. L’Apocalypse décrit elle aussi des êtres célestes célébrant sans cesse la sainteté divine (Ap 4,8). Ces deux visions distinctes éclairent la même adoration ; la formule de la Messe emploie « Deus Sabaoth », là où la Vulgate d’Isaïe dit « Deus exercituum ». [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/isa006.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/376.png). canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: If Christ's sacrifice is complete and infinitely acceptable, why does the priest first ask the Father to accept the offering?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The prayer addresses the Father through Christ, placing the sacrifice within the Church's visible communion. Guéranger reads its supplication as ecclesial action even while the celebrant speaks quietly. The mention of the Pope and appropriate bishop expresses communion; it is not merely administrative information added to a private devotion. The question of acceptance will return after the Consecration in Supra quae, but here the Canon is already concerned with the Church's peace, protection and unity.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Remembering the living [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).

This is a fitting moment to place one's family, benefactors and those in need before God. Their union with the offering is real, but it does not give them the ministerial priest's power to consecrate. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Whose sacrifice is this, and how can individual intentions belong to a single public offering?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The Memento brings particular persons before the Father and expressly names the faith and devotion of those around the altar. Guéranger's treatment notes how intercession extends to the circumstantes. The faithful's participation must be understood without confusing their spiritual union to the offering with the celebrant's power of sacramental Consecration. Private intentions enter the public liturgical prayer without turning the Canon into a collection of private liturgies.

canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Why name the saints within a sacrificial prayer addressed to the Father?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: Communicantes professes the Church's communion with Mary, Joseph, the apostles and martyrs; the faithful on earth are not a separate worshipping body from the saints in glory. Guéranger wrote before Joseph's insertion into the Roman Canon, and Lanslots's 1897 transcription likewise omits him. Both witnesses are valuable for historical comparison but cannot be presented as the wording of the liturgy after the 1962 insertion became effective. The Church's present text controls, while the history explains what changed.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: This oblation and our deliverance [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).

The extended hands are a gesture prescribed by the Roman rite; similarities to Old Testament laying-on of hands may illuminate their meaning but do not prove the historical origin of the Christian gesture. Les mains étendues constituent un geste prescrit par le rite romain ; l'analogie avec l'imposition des mains de l'Ancien Testament en éclaire le sens sans démontrer l'origine historique du geste chrétien. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: What do the priest's extended hands mean, and is the gesture derived from an Old Testament sacrificial act?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The prayer petitions acceptance, peace, deliverance from eternal condemnation and admission among the elect. Guéranger, St Alphonsus and Lanslots associate the extended hands with biblical imposition upon a victim. That is a meaningful traditional comparison, not proof that this Roman gesture originated by reenacting Leviticus. Leviticus 8:14 discusses hands upon the sin-offering bullock; Leviticus 16 also distinguishes the slain goat from the live scapegoat sent away. Torma's recent conflation requires correction rather than repetition.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The offering prepared for the mystery [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).

Under the 1962 ceremonial directions, he makes three signs of the Cross over both offerings, one over the Host at Corpus, and one over the chalice at Sanguis. These five signs precede, and are not themselves, the separate sacramental consecrations of bread and wine. [Roman Canon text and rubrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_and_rubrics_of_the_Roman_Canon) · [O’Connell, The Celebration of Mass (1962), p. 262](https://isidore.co/misc/Res%20pro%20Deo/ITOPL_OCR-layer-only/11a.%20Liturgy/d-The%20Celebration%20of%20Mass-%20O%27Connel%201962_OCR.pdf).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: L'offrande préparée au mystère [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).

Selon les prescriptions cérémonielles de 1962, il trace trois signes de croix sur les deux oblats, puis un sur l’Hostie au mot Corpus et un sur le calice au mot Sanguis. Ces cinq signes précèdent les consécrations sacramentelles distinctes du pain et du vin : ils ne constituent pas eux-mêmes ces consécrations. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Why does the Church ask God to make the offering 'reasonable' and acceptable immediately before Consecration?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: Guéranger relates rationabilem to the spiritual worship enjoined in Romans 12:1. The prayer asks that the oblation become for us Christ's Body and Blood. The five pre-Consecration crosses emphasize the actual Latin petitions but do not cause transubstantiation by themselves. Torma's description of the signs can be compared with the 1962 text; speculative interpretations of the five wounds are distinct from their rubrical timing and historical origin.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: At the words over the Host, Christ becomes truly present under the appearance of bread. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: At the Last Supper Jesus takes bread and declares, “This is my body,” commanding the apostles to do this in remembrance of him (1 Corinthians 11:23–24). At the heart of Mass the priest speaks the words of consecration in the person of Christ, and the bread truly becomes his Body. Calvary's sacrifice, offered once in history, is made sacramentally present rather than begun again as another historical event. The 1962 Roman formula has its own received liturgical wording. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Aux paroles sur l'Hostie, le Christ devient réellement présent sous l'apparence du pain. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: À la Cène, Jésus prend le pain et déclare : « Ceci est mon Corps », en ordonnant aux Apôtres de faire cela en mémoire de lui (1 Co 11,23–24). Au cœur de la Messe, le prêtre prononce les paroles de la consécration en la personne du Christ : le pain devient véritablement son Corps. Le sacrifice du Calvaire, offert une fois dans l’histoire, est rendu sacramentellement présent, non recommencé comme un nouvel événement. Le texte romain de 1962 possède sa formulation liturgique propre. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: At which instant is Christ truly present, and why are there several actions before and after it?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The institution narrative recalls the Last Supper, but the received Roman words and gestures are a liturgical text with history, not a verbatim transcript from one Evangelist. Guéranger comments on details such as Christ lifting His eyes. The Real Presence follows from the words of Consecration: the priest's immediate genuflection acknowledges what has already occurred. The elevation displays the consecrated Host for adoration; it does not make the bread become Christ's Body. Claims that every accompanying detail originates from a particular early Pope need manuscript evidence.
canonSourceCriticalStudy.transition: The chalice Consecration completes the two-species sacramental sign of the one sacrifice.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: At the words over the chalice, the Precious Blood becomes truly present under the appearance of wine. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk022.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: In giving the chalice to the apostles, Christ reveals that his Blood is poured out for the new covenant and the forgiveness of sins (Luke 22:20; Matthew 26:28). The consecration of the chalice directs the Church to Christ's redeeming self-offering and the real presence of his Precious Blood. In the 1962 Roman Canon the words “mysterium fidei” occur within the formula pronounced over the chalice, although they are not a verbatim phrase from Luke's institution account. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk022.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/389.png). [Doctrinal or patristic source](https://www.newadvent.org/summa/4075.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Aux paroles sur le calice, le Précieux Sang devient réellement présent sous l'apparence du vin. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/luk022.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: En donnant le calice aux Apôtres, le Christ révèle que son Sang est versé pour l’alliance nouvelle et la rémission des péchés (cf. Lc 22,20 ; Mt 26,28). À la consécration du calice, la Messe nous tourne vers l’offrande rédemptrice du Christ et la présence réelle de son Précieux Sang. Le Canon romain de 1962 inclut les mots « mysterium fidei » dans la formule prononcée sur le calice : ils appartiennent ici au texte liturgique reçu, sans être tirés mot pour mot du récit de saint Luc. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: How does Christ's Blood of the covenant become present without a second historical shedding of blood?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The Roman chalice formula relates the Blood of Christ to the new covenant and the forgiveness of sins. Its received 1962 wording includes mysterium fidei inside the consecratory formula. The Church's sacramental offering does not reproduce a second bloody death: the two species signify the sacrificial separation of Body and Blood while the whole risen Christ remains present under either species. Older commentators may offer symbolic explanations of cross-signs or narrative details, but no source may silently replace the 1962 formula with a harmonized Gospel paraphrase.
canonSourceCriticalStudy.transition: Once both Consecrations have occurred, the Canon explicitly names what the Church remembers and offers.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Unde et memores offers the consecrated Victim while remembering the Passion, Resurrection and Ascension. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: After the Consecration, the Canon remembers the Lord's blessed Passion, Resurrection and Ascension. St Paul teaches that by eating this Bread and drinking this Chalice the faithful proclaim the Lord's death until he comes (1 Corinthians 11:26). “Unde et memores” gives this living remembrance a place in the Church's offering: the whole Paschal victory of Christ is confessed within the one Eucharistic sacrifice. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/390.png). [Doctrinal or patristic source](https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/De_sacramentis_(Ambrosius)).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: L'Unde et memores offre la Victime consacrée en faisant mémoire de la Passion, de la Résurrection et de l'Ascension. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Après la consécration, le Canon proclame la mémoire de la Passion bienheureuse, de la Résurrection et de l’Ascension du Seigneur. Saint Paul enseigne qu’en mangeant ce Pain et en buvant ce Calice, les fidèles annoncent la mort du Seigneur jusqu’à ce qu’il vienne (1 Co 11,26). « Unde et memores » exprime cette mémoire vivante dans l’offrande de l’Église : toute la victoire pascale du Christ est confessée dans l’unique sacrifice eucharistique. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/390.png). [Commentaire doctrinal ou patristique](https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/De_sacramentis_(Ambrosius)).

canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Why remember Passion, Resurrection and Ascension within the sacrifice instead of stopping at Calvary?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The prayer does not isolate a moment of death. It explicitly commemorates the saving mysteries of Christ crucified, risen and ascended, and offers the gifts received from God. Guéranger explains that the signs made after Consecration do not bless Christ as though He required further sanctification; they recall His saving sacrifice. This is where a salvation-history narrative can reach beyond the historical Passion, while the liturgical commentary explains an actual Roman prayer rather than assigning arbitrary events to each cross.
canonSourceCriticalStudy.transition: The Canon then invokes the sacrifices named in ancient Scripture, now after Christ's presence upon the altar.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Abel's accepted offering is a biblical figure of sacrifice recalled in Supra quae. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen004.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: In “Supra quae,” the priest asks God to receive the Church's offering as he received that of righteous Abel. Genesis relates that Abel brought the firstborn of his flock, and God looked favourably upon his offering (Genesis 4:4). The Canon recalls the righteousness of the giver and God's acceptance, while the Church confidently petitions for the sacrifice of Christ. Abel is a biblical person expressly named by the prayer, not an event restaged at the altar. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen004.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/390.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: L'offrande agréée d'Abel est une figure biblique du sacrifice rappelée dans le Supra quae. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen004.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Dans « Supra quae », le prêtre demande à Dieu d’accueillir l’offrande de l’Église comme il accueillit celle du juste Abel. Selon la Genèse, Abel apporta les premiers-nés de son troupeau et Dieu regarda favorablement son sacrifice (Gn 4,4). Le Canon rappelle la fidélité du juste et l’agrément divin, afin que l’Église supplie avec confiance pour le sacrifice du Christ. Abel est ici un personnage biblique explicitement nommé, non le protagoniste d’une cérémonie reproduite à l’autel. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen004.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/390.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Abraham's willingness to offer Isaac foreshadows the Father's gift of the Son, without Isaac being slain. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen022.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: The Canon next recalls Abraham's sacrifice. God tests the patriarch's faith by asking for his beloved son Isaac, then stops Abraham before the child is killed (Genesis 22). Christian tradition sees in Abraham's obedience and intended offering a figure of the perfect self-gift accomplished in Christ. The Mass recalls a real episode of Genesis and understands it in the light of Jesus' redeeming sacrifice. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen022.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/390.png). [Second biblical passage](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/heb011.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: L'obéissance d'Abraham prêt à offrir Isaac préfigure le don du Fils, sans qu'Isaac ait été mis à mort. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen022.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Le Canon évoque ensuite le sacrifice d’Abraham. Dieu éprouve la foi du patriarche en lui demandant Isaac, son fils bien-aimé, puis arrête sa main avant que l’enfant soit immolé (Gn 22). La tradition chrétienne reconnaît dans cette obéissance et cette offrande annoncée une figure de l'offrande parfaite du Christ à son Père. La Messe rappelle donc un épisode réel de la Genèse, tout en l’éclairant par le sacrifice rédempteur de Jésus. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen022.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/390.png). [Deuxième passage biblique](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/heb011.htm).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Melchisedech's bread and wine illuminate the Eucharistic sacrifice as a traditional biblical figure. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen014.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram (Genesis 14:18–20). The Canon names him among the ancient figures of an offering pleasing to God. Hebrews explains how his priesthood sheds light on Christ's (Hebrews 7). Christian interpretation sees a Eucharistic foreshadowing in the bread and wine, although Genesis itself does not explicitly describe those elements being sacrificed. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen014.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/391.png). [Hebrews 7](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/heb007.htm) · [Cyprian, Epistle 62](https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/050662.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Le pain et le vin de Melchisédech éclairent le Sacrifice eucharistique par une figure biblique traditionnelle. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen014.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Melchisédech, roi de Salem et prêtre du Dieu Très-Haut, accueille Abram avec du pain et du vin et le bénit (Gn 14,18–20). Le Canon le nomme parmi les figures anciennes de l’offrande agréable à Dieu. L’épître aux Hébreux explique en outre pourquoi son sacerdoce éclaire celui du Christ (He 7). La lecture chrétienne voit dans le pain et le vin une préfiguration eucharistique ; le récit de la Genèse, pris seul, ne décrit pas explicitement leur immolation sacrificielle. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/gen014.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/391.png). [Hébreux 7](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/heb007.htm) · [Cyprien, Lettre 62](https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/050662.htm).

canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Why ask that the Eucharistic offering be received like the gifts of Abel, Abraham and Melchisedech, if it is infinitely greater?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: Guéranger and Gihr confront this as a real theological problem rather than a decorative list of Old Testament stories. Gihr, drawing on St Thomas, locates the comparison in the faith and devotion of the earlier offerers and God's favourable regard, not in equality between victims. Abel's faith, Abraham's obedience and Melchisedech's priesthood are distinct interpretive avenues. Genesis says Melchisedech brought forth bread and wine; Gihr's assertion that he sacrificed them is subsequent Christian interpretation, not the Bible's direct narration. His hypothesis of fire consuming Abel's offering likewise exceeds Genesis 4.
canonSourceCriticalStudy.transition: The question of acceptance leads into the more difficult language of the angel, the heavenly altar and participation in heavenly blessing.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The holy Angel and the heavenly altar [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: In Supplices te rogamus the priest asks that the offering be borne before God's majesty by the hands of his holy Angel, so that communicants may receive heavenly blessing and grace. St Thomas Aquinas explains both an angel presenting the prayers of priest and people and a spiritual interpretation referring to Christ, the Angel of great counsel. These are interpretations, not a dogmatic identification imposed by the prayer. Aquinas explicitly denies that the consecrated species or Christ's true Body are physically carried from the altar to heaven. [Roman Canon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_and_rubrics_of_the_Roman_Canon) · [St Thomas, Summa theologiae III, q. 83, a. 4, ad 9](https://www.newadvent.org/summa/4083.htm#article4) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Dans Supplices te rogamus, le prêtre demande que l'offrande soit portée devant la majesté divine par les mains du saint Ange de Dieu, afin que ceux qui communient reçoivent la bénédiction et la grâce célestes. Saint Thomas d'Aquin explique à la fois l'intervention d'un ange présentant les prières du prêtre et du peuple, et une interprétation spirituelle rapportant l'Ange au Christ, l'Ange du grand conseil. Il s'agit d'interprétations, non d'une identification dogmatique imposée par la prière. Saint Thomas exclut expressément que les espèces consacrées ou le vrai Corps du Christ soient matériellement transportés de l'autel au ciel. [Canon romain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_and_rubrics_of_the_Roman_Canon) · [Saint Thomas, Somme théologique III, q. 83, a. 4, ad 9](https://www.newadvent.org/summa/4083.htm#article4) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/).

canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Who is the holy Angel, and what does it mean for the offering to be borne to the heavenly altar?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: Guéranger interprets the Angel christologically; Lanslots juxtaposes that account with other angelic readings and acknowledges uncertainty. St Alphonsus reports a Christological explanation from a French predecessor but favours the reading associated with St Thomas, concerning the angelic presentation of the Church's prayers. These are distinguishable authorial positions, not several synonyms. St Thomas expressly resists imagining that Christ's physical Body or the consecrated species leave the altar to be carried to heaven. The petition concerns heavenly communion and blessing, not Eucharistic relocation.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The faithful departed [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: The Memento for the dead prays for those who have gone before us in faith and rest in peace, asking God to grant light, refreshment and peace. To pray for the dead is an act of charity and hope in God's mercy, not an attempt to declare the final state of an individual soul. Historical rules about public naming in the Canon must be kept distinct from private intercession and from the normative rubrics of the particular celebration. [1962 rite](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/) · [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1th004.htm).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Le Mémento des défunts prie pour ceux qui nous ont précédés dans la foi et reposent dans la paix, afin que Dieu leur accorde la lumière, le rafraîchissement et la paix. Prier pour les morts est un acte de charité et d'espérance en la miséricorde divine, non une déclaration sur le sort éternel d'une âme particulière. Les anciennes règles sur les noms publiquement mentionnés au Canon se distinguent de la prière privée et des rubriques applicables. [Rite de 1962](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/) · [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1th004.htm).

canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: What can the Eucharistic Sacrifice mean for those who have died, and how does naming them differ from private prayer?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The Canon commends the faithful departed to God, asking for a place of refreshment, light and peace. Guéranger's interpretation of the signum fidei makes one historic link to Christian initiation; it should not displace the text's own wording. Lanslots distinguishes the rules and history of public liturgical naming from the possibility of private intercession. We should explain the Church's prayer for the dead without pretending the celebrant knows the final state of any particular soul or collapsing rubrical diptychs into the personal intentions of every attendee.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Nobis quoque: the sinner's hope [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: At Nobis quoque peccatoribus, the celebrant asks that sinners who hope in God's manifold mercies receive some part in fellowship with the apostles and martyrs. The petition is marked by humility: the promised reward is sought not by presuming on personal merit, but by asking pardon and admittance through Christ. It gives the faithful language for the hope of conversion during the silent Canon. [1962 rite](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Nobis quoque : l'espérance du pécheur [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Au Nobis quoque peccatoribus, le célébrant demande que les pécheurs qui espèrent en la multitude des miséricordes divines aient part à la société des apôtres et des martyrs. La demande est humble : la récompense n'est pas revendiquée au titre du mérite personnel, mais implorée par le pardon et l'admission en Jésus-Christ. Les fidèles trouvent ainsi une prière d'espérance et de conversion au cœur du Canon silencieux. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Why does a Canon full of saints and divine glory return to the confession of one's own sinfulness?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The priest breaks the prevailing silence of the Canon at its opening words, strikes his breast, and asks for fellowship with apostles and martyrs. The decisive words reject the presumption of deserving such a reward through one's own merit. Guéranger observes the gesture and reports practices of the faithful, but historical custom must not be imposed as universal posture or action in a 1962 congregation. The theological logic is not embarrassment after Consecration: the Eucharistic offering establishes precisely the ground of hope for sinners.
canonSourceCriticalStudy.transition: The Canon's closing sentences turn from petition to praise through the one mediator, Christ.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Every good gift through Christ [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: Per quem haec omnia acknowledges that through Christ God creates, sanctifies, gives life, blesses and bestows all these good things. The priest makes three signs of the Cross over the Host and chalice at sanctificas, vivificas and benedicis; these do not consecrate again. The precise referent of haec omnia has received differing historical interpretations, including a possible association with blessings of material gifts in earlier usage. That proposed origin should not be taught as certain or imposed on the 1962 rite. [Roman Canon text and rubrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_and_rubrics_of_the_Roman_Canon) · [Catholic Encyclopedia, Canon of the Mass (historical interpretation)](https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/03255c.htm).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Dans Per quem haec omnia, l'Église reconnaît que, par le Christ, Dieu crée, sanctifie, vivifie, bénit et nous accorde tous ces biens. Le prêtre trace trois signes de croix sur l'Hostie et le calice aux mots sanctificas, vivificas et benedicis ; il ne s'agit pas de nouvelles consécrations. Le sens précis de haec omnia a donné lieu à diverses interprétations historiques, dont un rapprochement possible avec d'anciennes bénédictions de biens matériels. Cette hypothèse d'origine ne doit pas être présentée comme certaine ni confondue avec les rubriques de 1962. canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: What are 'all these good things' and why does the priest make signs of the Cross after Consecration?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The words name God as the giver of creation, sanctification, life and blessing through Christ. Guéranger recalls a historical association with blessings of additional material gifts; this requires evidence rather than a confident reconstruction of what every ancient Mass celebrated. The three crosses belong to the actual 1962 ceremonial sequence but are not a repeated Consecration. This prayer therefore juxtaposes the whole created order and the Eucharistic gift without authorizing picturesque invented rites.

canonSourceCriticalStudy.question: Why does the Canon end with another elevation, and what is being offered to the Father?
canonSourceCriticalStudy.authorDrivenEnglishExplanation: The words glorify the Father through Christ, with Him and in Him, in the unity of the Holy Ghost. Guéranger distinguishes the small elevation associated with this doxology from the ostension immediately after each Consecration. The crosses and actions have exact 1962 positions; they neither reconsecrate the sacred species nor restage another event in Christ's earthly life. The theological movement is complete: the Church's prayer, united to Christ's own self-offering, reaches its doxological conclusion.

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The Pater noster places the Lord's own prayer immediately before Communion. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat006.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: After the Canon, the priest prays the words Christ taught his disciples. The Our Father joins adoration of God's name, longing for his kingdom, daily bread, forgiveness and deliverance from evil (Matthew 6:9–13; Luke 11:2–4). The printed 1962 Latin Missal has “panem nostrum cotidianum,” corresponding in sense to Luke's “quotidianum”; the Clementine Matthew reads “supersubstantialem.” The Lord's Prayer is thus proclaimed in its received Roman liturgical form. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat006.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/395.png).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Le Pater noster place la prière enseignée par le Seigneur juste avant la Communion. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat006.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Après le Canon, le prêtre récite la prière que Jésus a enseignée à ses disciples. Le Notre Père unit l’adoration du nom divin, l’attente du Règne, la demande du pain, le pardon et la délivrance du mal (Mt 6,9–13 ; Lc 11,2–4). Dans le texte latin du Missel de 1962, on lit « panem nostrum cotidianum », comme le sens du « quotidianum » de Luc ; la Vulgate clémentine de Matthieu dit « supersubstantialem ». La prière demeure celle du Seigneur, sous sa forme liturgique romaine. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat006.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/395.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Deliverance, peace, and the commingling [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: Libera nos expands the last petition of the Lord's Prayer, asking deliverance from past, present and future evils through the saints' intercession. The Fraction breaks the consecrated Host; the Pax Domini wishes the Lord's peace. At the commingling a small particle enters the chalice: the word consecratio in that prayer does not mean a second Eucharistic Consecration. The successive actions possess distinct meanings and must not be collapsed into one invented gesture. At Requiem Mass, the prayer Domine Iesu Christe, qui dixisti Apostolis tuis is omitted and the kiss of peace is not given. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Délivrance, paix et mélange des espèces [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Le Libera nos développe la dernière demande du Notre Père, implorant la délivrance des maux passés, présents et futurs avec l'intercession des saints. La fraction divise l'Hostie consacrée ; le Pax Domini souhaite la paix du Seigneur. Lors du mélange, une parcelle est déposée dans le calice : le mot consecratio de cette prière ne signifie pas une seconde Consécration eucharistique. Ces gestes successifs ont leur sens propre et ne doivent pas être confondus. À la messe des défunts, la prière Domine Iesu Christe, qui dixisti Apostolis tuis est omise et le baiser de paix n'est pas donné. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The Agnus Dei invokes Christ as the Lamb who takes away the world's sin. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh001.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: John the Baptist points to Jesus as “the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world” (John 1:29). Before Communion the Church addresses Christ as the sacrificial Lamb who saves, asking first for mercy and then peace. At Masses for the Dead the petitions ask instead for the souls' rest: “dona eis requiem” and finally “dona eis requiem sempiternam.” The celebrant also omits the ordinary breast strikes at the Requiem Agnus Dei. The same biblical title thus serves differing liturgical intentions. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh001.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/400.png). Avant la Communion, l’Église s’adresse au Christ comme à la victime offerte pour le salut et implore sa miséricorde puis sa paix. Le prêtre omet également les frappements de poitrine habituels à l'Agnus Dei des défunts. Le même titre biblique nourrit ainsi des intentions liturgiques différentes. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The priest repeats the centurion's act of humble faith before his own Communion. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat008.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: A centurion acknowledges Jesus' authority and says he is unworthy to receive him under his roof: one word from the Lord can heal his servant (Matthew 8:8). Before Communion the priest takes up this profession of trust and humility: “Domine, non sum dignus,” asking for the healing of his own soul. The Gospel speaks of “puer meus,” the servant; the Mass applies the petition to “anima mea,” the communicant's soul. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat008.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/402.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Un centurion reconnaît l’autorité de Jésus et déclare qu’il n’est pas digne de le recevoir sous son toit ; une seule parole du Seigneur peut guérir son serviteur (Mt 8,8). Avant la Communion, le prêtre reprend cette confession de confiance et d’humilité : « Domine, non sum dignus », puis demande la guérison de son âme. L’Évangile parle du serviteur, « puer meus » ; la Messe applique la demande au communiant, « anima mea ». [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/mat008.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/402.png).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Christ's promised peace is invoked for the unity of his Church before Communion. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh014.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: Before Communion, the prayer “Domine Iesu Christe, qui dixisti Apostolis tuis” takes up Jesus' promise: “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you” (John 14:27). The priest asks the Lord to look not upon human sins but upon the faith of his Church, granting her unity and peace. Christ's peace is a gift deeper than the mere absence of conflict. Under the 1962 rite this prayer and the kiss of peace are omitted at Masses for the Dead. [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh014.htm) · [Original 1962 Roman Missal page](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/400.png). [1962 Requiem rubrics](https://1962ordo.today/1962-rubrics/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: La paix promise par le Christ est implorée pour l'unité de son Église avant la Communion. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh014.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Avant la Communion, la prière « Domine Iesu Christe, qui dixisti Apostolis tuis » reprend la promesse de Jésus aux siens : « Je vous laisse la paix, je vous donne ma paix » (Jn 14,27). Le prêtre demande alors au Seigneur de ne pas regarder les péchés de chacun, mais la foi de son Église, et de lui accorder l’unité et la paix. Cette paix est un don du Christ, plus profond que la seule absence de conflit. Cette prière et le baiser de paix sont omis aux Messes des défunts selon le rite de 1962. [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/joh014.htm) · [Missel romain de 1962, page originale](https://gregobase.selapa.net/sources/42/400.png). [Rubriques de la Messe des défunts](https://1962ordo.today/1962-rubrics/).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Se préparer à recevoir le Seigneur [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Lorsque la Communion doit être distribuée aux fidèles, la liturgie prévoit une préparation distincte des prières privées récitées auparavant par le prêtre. L'« Ecce Agnus Dei » et le « Domine, non sum dignus » des fidèles invitent à une profession de foi et d'humilité devant le Christ réellement présent. Le second Confiteor, présent dans des usages anciens ou locaux, n'est pas prescrit pour la distribution de la Communion par le Missel de 1962 et ne doit donc pas être présenté comme une obligation liturgique universelle ; les répétitions distinctes du prêtre ne doivent pas non plus être transférées à l'assemblée. [Rite de 1962](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm). studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: Communion is a sacred participation [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: The faithful who receive Holy Communion truly receive the living Christ, whose sacrifice has been offered on the altar. Worthy reception asks for faith, preparation and reverence; St Paul warns against eating and drinking unworthily. Communion of the faithful is highly recommended, but the Eucharistic sacrifice does not depend upon every member of the congregation communicating. The actual distribution takes place only when communicants are present and according to the applicable rite. [1962 rite](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: La Communion est une participation sacrée [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Les fidèles qui communient reçoivent réellement le Christ vivant, dont le Sacrifice a été offert à l'autel. Une réception digne demande la foi, la préparation et le respect ; saint Paul avertit contre une communion indigne. La Communion des fidèles est vivement recommandée, mais l'existence du Sacrifice eucharistique ne dépend pas de la communion de chaque assistant. La distribution a lieu lorsque des communiants sont présents, selon le rite applicable. [Rite de 1962](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Écriture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/1co011.htm).

studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: What we have received [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: During the ablutions, the celebrant receives the prescribed purifications and prays that what has passed his lips may be received with a pure mind and bring an enduring spiritual remedy. The Communion antiphon belongs to the variable Proper and cannot be supplied from one unchanging example. This part of the Mass teaches that the sacramental gift should bear fruit beyond the brief moments of Communion. [1962 rite](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: Ce que nous avons reçu [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Pendant les ablutions, le célébrant accomplit les purifications prescrites et demande que ce qu'il a reçu de la bouche soit accueilli avec une âme pure et lui procure un remède durable. L'antienne de Communion appartient au Propre variable et ne peut être remplacée par un exemple uniforme. Cette partie de la Messe enseigne que le don sacramentel doit porter du fruit bien au-delà des instants de la Communion. studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishShort: The Church gives thanks [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalEnglishDeep: In the Postcommunion prayer the Church asks that the Sacrament received accomplish its fruit in those who have shared in the holy mysteries. This liturgical thanksgiving is not the same as a person's own thanksgiving after Mass: both have a proper place. The particular words are those appointed for the day, with any lawful additional orations; the generic explanation should not replace them. [1962 rite](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/) · [Guéranger](https://www.domgueranger.net/explication-des-prieres-de-la-sainte-messe-2/) · [Scripture](https://www.newadvent.org/bible/col003.htm).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchShort: L'Église rend grâce [Source](https://archive.ccwatershed.org/pdfs/5276-ritus-servandus-translated-english/download/).
studyOfMassExistingDrafts.originalFrenchDeep: Dans la Postcommunion, l'Église demande que le Sacrement reçu produise ses fruits chez ceux qui ont participé aux saints mystères. Cette action de grâces liturgique ne se confond pas avec l'action de grâces personnelle après la Messe : chacune a sa place. Les paroles sont celles qui sont prescrites pour le jour, avec les oraisons supplémentaires permises ; une explication générale ne les remplace pas.
